### BEGIN PAGE
title: Coffee & Tea Glossary | Gray Cup
url: https://graycup.in/glossary
### END PAGE

A glossary of coffee and tea terms - processing methods, varietals, tea styles, and brewing methods, explained in plain language.

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is AeroPress? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/aeropress
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

The AeroPress is a compact, manual brewer that steeps coffee grounds in hot water for a short time, then uses a plunger to push the brew through a paper filter with gentle air pressure. It's fast, portable, and forgiving, and can produce anything from an espresso-like concentrate to a lighter, filter-style cup depending on the recipe used.

### Related Terms

[Pour Over](https://graycup.in/glossary/pour-over)[French Press](https://graycup.in/glossary/french-press)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Arabica? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/arabica
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Arabica (Coffea arabica) is the coffee species most associated with specialty and single-origin coffee. It's grown at higher altitudes, is more delicate to farm, and produces a more complex, aromatic cup with brighter acidity compared to Robusta - which is why it commands a premium and dominates specialty coffee menus.

### Related Terms

[Robusta](https://graycup.in/glossary/robusta)[Varietal](https://graycup.in/glossary/varietal)[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Blend? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/blend
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

A blend is coffee made by combining beans from more than one origin, varietal, or processing method. Blending lets a roaster balance sweetness, acidity, and body across batches, and deliver a consistent flavour profile year-round even as any single origin's harvest changes.

### Products with Blend

[Dooars & Assam Tea](https://graycup.in/products/dooars-assam-tea)[Filter Coffee (70% Arabica, 30% Robusta)](https://graycup.in/products/filter-coffee-arabica-robusta)[Filter Coffee (70% Arabica, 30% Chicory)](https://graycup.in/products/filter-coffee-arabica-chicory)[Vienna Roast Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/vienna-roast-coffee)

### Related Terms

[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)[Varietal](https://graycup.in/glossary/varietal)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Cold Brew? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/cold-brew
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Cold brew is made by steeping coarsely ground coffee in cold or room-temperature water for 12-24 hours, rather than using heat to extract flavour quickly. The slow, cold extraction produces a smoother, naturally sweeter, less acidic concentrate, usually diluted with water, milk, or ice before drinking.

### Related Terms

[French Press](https://graycup.in/glossary/french-press)[South Indian Filter Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/south-indian-filter)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is CTC Tea? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/ctc-tea
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

CTC stands for Crush, Tear, Curl - a tea processing method where leaves are passed through rollers that crush, tear, and curl them into small, uniform granules. CTC tea brews faster and stronger than loose leaf tea, making it well suited to milk tea and chai, and is the dominant style produced in Assam and the Dooars.

### Products with CTC Tea

[Dooars & Assam Tea](https://graycup.in/products/dooars-assam-tea)[Giddapahar Darjeeling Orthodox](https://graycup.in/products/giddapahar-darjeeling-orthodox)

### Related Terms

[Orthodox Tea](https://graycup.in/glossary/orthodox-tea)[Loose Leaf Tea](https://graycup.in/glossary/loose-leaf-tea)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Cupping? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/cupping
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Cupping is the standardized method coffee professionals use to taste and evaluate coffee - brewing a set ratio of coarsely ground coffee to hot water in a bowl, breaking the crust to smell the aroma, then slurping the brew across the palate to score its aroma, acidity, body, sweetness, and aftertaste. It's how coffees are graded and how buyers and roasters compare lots before purchasing.

### Related Terms

[Speciality Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/speciality-coffee)[Flavour Notes](https://graycup.in/glossary/flavour-notes)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Espresso? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/espresso
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Espresso is made by forcing hot water through finely ground, tightly packed coffee at high pressure, producing a small, concentrated shot topped with crema. It's the base for most café drinks - lattes, cappuccinos, and Americanos are all built on an espresso shot.

### Related Terms

[Moka Pot](https://graycup.in/glossary/moka-pot)[French Press](https://graycup.in/glossary/french-press)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Estate Coffee? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/estate-coffee
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Estate coffee is grown, harvested, and often processed entirely on one specific, named plantation - as opposed to being pooled together from many smallholder farms in a region. Because every step happens under one estate's practices, estate coffee usually offers more consistency and traceability than a general regional lot.

### Related Terms

[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)[Shade-Grown Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/shade-grown)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Flavour Notes? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/flavour-notes
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Flavour notes describe the tastes and aromas you might pick up in a cup - similar to how tasting notes work for wine or whisky. They come from a coffee's origin, processing method, and roast, and are meant as a guide to what to expect rather than a guarantee of what you'll taste, since palates and brewing methods vary.

### Related Terms

[Cupping](https://graycup.in/glossary/cupping)[Washed Process](https://graycup.in/glossary/washed-process)[Natural Process](https://graycup.in/glossary/natural-process)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is French Press? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/french-press
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

A French Press brews coffee by steeping coarse grounds directly in hot water, then separating them with a metal mesh plunger. Because a metal filter (rather than paper) is used, the coffee's natural oils stay in the cup, giving a fuller body and richer mouthfeel than filtered methods.

### Related Terms

[Cold Brew](https://graycup.in/glossary/cold-brew)[Pour Over](https://graycup.in/glossary/pour-over)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Honey Process (HSD)? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/honey-process
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Honey processing (also called honey sundried, or HSD) sits between washed and natural processing. Some or all of the sticky mucilage is left on the parchment during sun-drying instead of being washed off, which balances brightness with sweetness. The result is typically a fuller-bodied cup than washed coffee, with more clarity than a fully natural-processed one.

### Products with Honey Process (HSD)

[Koraput, Odisha Honey Sundried Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-hsd-coffee)[Attikan Honey Sundried Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/attikan-estate-honey-sundried-coffee)

### Related Terms

[Washed Process](https://graycup.in/glossary/washed-process)[Natural Process](https://graycup.in/glossary/natural-process)[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Loose Leaf Tea? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/loose-leaf-tea
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Loose leaf tea is whole or large-piece tea leaves sold without being packed into bags. Because the leaves have more room to unfurl and release their oils during steeping, loose leaf tea generally delivers more flavour and aroma than bagged tea, and the same leaves can often be steeped more than once.

### Products with Loose Leaf Tea

[Dooars & Assam Tea](https://graycup.in/products/dooars-assam-tea)[Giddapahar Darjeeling Orthodox](https://graycup.in/products/giddapahar-darjeeling-orthodox)

### Related Terms

[Orthodox Tea](https://graycup.in/glossary/orthodox-tea)[CTC Tea](https://graycup.in/glossary/ctc-tea)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Moka Pot? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/moka-pot
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

A Moka Pot is a stovetop brewer with three chambers: water at the bottom, finely ground coffee in the middle basket, and the brewed coffee collecting at the top. As the water heats, steam pressure pushes it up through the grounds, producing a strong, concentrated cup closer to espresso than drip coffee, without needing an espresso machine.

### Related Terms

[Espresso](https://graycup.in/glossary/espresso)[South Indian Filter Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/south-indian-filter)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Natural Process? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/natural-process
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Natural (or dry) processing is the oldest coffee processing method: whole cherries are dried in the sun with the fruit still intact, then hulled afterwards to remove the dried skin and pulp. Because the bean absorbs sugars and flavour compounds from the fruit while drying, natural-processed coffees tend to be fruitier, more full-bodied, and sometimes wine-like in the cup.

### Products with Natural Process

[Koraput, Odisha Naturals Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-natural-coffee)[Halflong Assam Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/halflong-assam-coffee)

### Related Terms

[Washed Process](https://graycup.in/glossary/washed-process)[Honey Process (HSD)](https://graycup.in/glossary/honey-process)[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Orthodox Tea? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/orthodox-tea
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Orthodox tea is processed using traditional methods - withering, rolling, and oxidising whole or large-leaf tea by hand or with gentler machinery, rather than mechanically fragmenting it like CTC processing does. Keeping the leaf more intact generally produces a more nuanced, complex cup, prized in regions like Darjeeling.

### Products with Orthodox Tea

[Dooars & Assam Tea](https://graycup.in/products/dooars-assam-tea)[Giddapahar Darjeeling Orthodox](https://graycup.in/products/giddapahar-darjeeling-orthodox)

### Related Terms

[CTC Tea](https://graycup.in/glossary/ctc-tea)[Loose Leaf Tea](https://graycup.in/glossary/loose-leaf-tea)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Pour Over? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/pour-over
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Pour over is a manual brewing method where hot water is poured in a controlled, circular motion over coffee grounds sitting in a paper or metal filter cone. The slower, gravity-fed extraction and paper filtration (in most setups) produce a cleaner, brighter cup that highlights a coffee's origin character.

### Related Terms

[French Press](https://graycup.in/glossary/french-press)[AeroPress](https://graycup.in/glossary/aeropress)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Robusta? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/robusta
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Robusta (Coffea canephora) is a hardier coffee species that grows at lower altitudes and resists pests better than Arabica. It has roughly double the caffeine content and a bolder, earthier, more bitter cup - it's commonly used in espresso blends for crema and body, and in instant coffee.

### Related Terms

[Arabica](https://graycup.in/glossary/arabica)[Varietal](https://graycup.in/glossary/varietal)[Blend](https://graycup.in/glossary/blend)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Shade-Grown Coffee? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/shade-grown
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Shade-grown coffee is cultivated under a canopy of native trees instead of in direct, cleared sunlight. The shade slows down how fast the cherries ripen, which gives the beans more time to develop sugars and flavour compounds - it's also better for biodiversity, since the tree canopy supports birds and other wildlife that clear-cut plantations don't.

### Related Terms

[Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/estate-coffee)[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Single Origin Coffee? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Single origin coffee comes from one specific estate, farm, or growing region, rather than being blended with beans from multiple sources. Because the beans share the same soil, altitude, and climate, single origin coffee tends to have a more distinct, traceable flavour profile that reflects the terroir of that specific place.

### Products with Single Origin Coffee

[Giddapahar Darjeeling Orthodox](https://graycup.in/products/giddapahar-darjeeling-orthodox)[Koraput, Odisha Honey Sundried Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-hsd-coffee)[Koraput, Odisha Naturals Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-natural-coffee)[Koraput, Odisha Washed Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-washed-coffee)

### Related Terms

[Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/estate-coffee)[Varietal](https://graycup.in/glossary/varietal)[Washed Process](https://graycup.in/glossary/washed-process)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is South Indian Filter Coffee? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/south-indian-filter
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

South Indian filter coffee is brewed by slowly dripping hot water through finely ground coffee (often with chicory) in a traditional two-chamber metal filter, called a filter kaapi set. The strong decoction is then mixed with hot milk and sugar and traditionally poured back and forth between two cups ("meter coffee") to build a frothy top.

### Products with South Indian Filter Coffee

[Koraput, Odisha Honey Sundried Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-hsd-coffee)[Koraput, Odisha Naturals Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-natural-coffee)[Koraput, Odisha Washed Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-washed-coffee)[Karadykan Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/karadykan-estate-coffee)

### Related Terms

[Moka Pot](https://graycup.in/glossary/moka-pot)[Cold Brew](https://graycup.in/glossary/cold-brew)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Speciality Coffee? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/speciality-coffee
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Speciality coffee refers to the highest quality grade of coffee, typically defect-free green beans that score 80 or above out of 100 on a professional cupping evaluation. It sits above "commercial" grade coffee, which is perfectly drinkable but has more inconsistency, defects, or a simpler flavour profile.

### Related Terms

[Cupping](https://graycup.in/glossary/cupping)[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Varietal? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/varietal
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

A varietal is the specific genetic variety of coffee plant a bean was grown from - similar to how a grape varietal shapes a wine. Varietals like SLN 9 or SLN 795 differ in flavour potential, disease resistance, and yield, and are one of the biggest factors (alongside processing and terroir) behind why two coffees can taste so different.

### Related Terms

[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)[Arabica](https://graycup.in/glossary/arabica)[Robusta](https://graycup.in/glossary/robusta)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: What is Washed Process? | Gray Cup Glossary
url: https://graycup.in/glossary/washed-process
### END PAGE

[All Glossary Terms](https://graycup.in/glossary)

Washed (or wet) processing is a coffee processing method where the outer fruit skin and sticky mucilage are completely removed from the bean using water, then the parchment is dried separately. Because none of the fruit stays on the bean during drying, washed coffees tend to have a cleaner, brighter, more consistent cup - the flavour comes through more clearly since less fruit sugar interacts with the bean.

### Products with Washed Process

[Koraput, Odisha Washed Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-washed-coffee)[Karadykan Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/karadykan-estate-coffee)[Biccode Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/products/biccode-estate-coffee)[Filter Coffee (70% Arabica, 30% Robusta)](https://graycup.in/products/filter-coffee-arabica-robusta)

### Related Terms

[Natural Process](https://graycup.in/glossary/natural-process)[Honey Process (HSD)](https://graycup.in/glossary/honey-process)[Single Origin Coffee](https://graycup.in/glossary/single-origin)

### Top 5 Black Coffees for Liver Health

Research links black coffee to better liver enzyme levels and lower risk of liver disease. Here are 5 black coffees worth keeping in your rotation.

30 July 20266 min read

](https://graycup.in/guides/black-coffee-liver-health)[

CoffeeHealthFatty Liver

### Best Black Coffee Brand for Fatty Liver

Fatty liver disease is linked to lower coffee consumption in several studies. Here's what the research says and the best black coffees to build into a daily routine.

10 August 20266 min read

](https://graycup.in/guides/best-black-coffee-for-fatty-liver)

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: Best Black Coffee Brand for Fatty Liver | Gray Cup Guides
url: https://graycup.in/guides/best-black-coffee-for-fatty-liver
### END PAGE

Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) - now often called MASLD - is one of the most common liver conditions worldwide, and diet plays a big role in managing it. Coffee is one of the few beverages that shows up consistently in this research: several studies have linked regular coffee drinking to a lower risk of developing fatty liver, less severe fibrosis in people who already have it, and better liver enzyme readings overall. The effect seems strongest with black coffee, since the added milk, cream and sugar in most coffee drinks work against the same metabolic goals coffee is being credited for.

This isn't a substitute for medical advice or treatment - fatty liver needs to be managed with a doctor, especially around weight, alcohol and sugar intake. But if you're already looking to add black coffee to your routine, the beans you actually enjoy drinking black make the difference between a habit that sticks and one that doesn't.

Here's what to look for in a black coffee brand, and five picks worth trying.

### What Makes a Coffee "Good" for Fatty Liver

There's no single fatty-liver coffee brand backed by clinical trials - the research is about coffee as a category, particularly filtered, brewed black coffee drunk consistently over time. A few things matter more than the label:

*   **Ground, not instant.** Instant coffee goes through more processing, which reduces the chlorogenic acid and other plant polyphenols thought to be behind coffee's liver benefits. Ground, freshly brewed coffee retains more of them.
*   **No added sugar or cream.** Fatty liver management is closely tied to reducing added sugar and saturated fat - pouring both into your coffee undoes a lot of the point.
*   **Something you'll drink every day.** The studies showing benefit are about habitual intake over months and years, not one cup on a good day. A coffee that's too bitter or harsh to drink black consistently isn't the right choice, no matter what's in it.

With that in mind, here are five black coffees worth keeping in rotation.

### 1\. Koraput, Odisha Washed Coffee

A clean, bright single-origin from the hills of Koraput, Odisha. The washed process removes the cherry skin and mucilage before drying, giving a well-defined, low-bitterness cup that's easy to drink black without needing sugar or milk to soften it - useful when you're trying to cut both from your diet.

[![Koraput, Odisha Washed Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput-washed.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-washed-coffee)

### 2\. Basic Black Coffee

Our everyday, no-frills blend, built to be brewed any way you like without fuss. If the goal is simply "drink black coffee every day, without overthinking it," this is the most practical option - a reliable, mellow cup you'll actually finish, which matters more for a daily habit than any single origin story.

[![Basic Black Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fground-coffee.png&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/basic-black-coffee)

### 3\. Karadykan Estate Coffee

Grown under native shade cover, this single-estate Arabica has a balanced cup with notes of chocolate, citrus and orange. It's smooth enough to drink black two or three times a day without fatigue, which is closer to the intake levels the fatty liver studies actually looked at.

[![Karadykan Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/karadykan-estate-coffee)

### 4\. Biccode Estate Coffee

A washed-process Arabica (SLN 795) with notes of lemon zest, cacao nibs and caramel. It's medium-intensity rather than sharp or acidic, so it sits easier on an empty stomach - a common concern for people cutting back on sugar and looking for a gentler black coffee to start the day with.

[![Biccode Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/biccode-estate-coffee)

### 5\. Halflong Assam Coffee

A single-origin Arabica from the North Cachar Hills of Assam, with mild acidity and a soft, earthy sweetness. It's one of the gentlest coffees in our range, which makes it a good entry point if you're new to drinking coffee black and finding brighter, more acidic cups hard to get through.

[![Halflong Assam Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/halflong-assam-coffee)

### How Much Coffee, and How to Brew It

Most of the studies showing a benefit for fatty liver looked at people drinking around 2 to 3 cups of coffee a day - more wasn't shown to add further benefit, and too much late in the day will just cost you sleep. Filter or pour-over both work fine; there's no strong evidence that brew method changes the benefit, only that ground, brewed coffee outperforms instant.

### A Few Practical Notes

*   **Skip the sugar, skip the cream.** If fatty liver is the reason you're drinking black coffee, adding sugar and saturated fat back in works against the point.
*   **Consistency matters more than the specific bean.** Any of the coffees above work - the research is about habitual intake, not a single miracle brand.
*   **This supports a plan, it isn't the plan.** Weight management, cutting added sugar and alcohol, and regular checkups with a doctor are what actually treat fatty liver. Coffee is a small, low-cost addition on top of that.

* * *

If you already drink coffee, taking it black - and picking beans you genuinely enjoy that way - is one of the easiest dietary habits to keep. None of this is medical advice, so talk to a doctor about managing fatty liver directly, but there's no downside to making your daily coffee a black one.

### BEGIN PAGE
title: Top 5 Black Coffees for Liver Health | Gray Cup Guides
url: https://graycup.in/guides/black-coffee-liver-health
### END PAGE

Coffee is one of the most studied beverages when it comes to liver health, and black coffee - no milk, no sugar - is where most of the benefit shows up. Multiple observational studies have linked regular coffee drinking to lower levels of liver enzymes (like ALT and GGT), a reduced risk of fatty liver disease, and even a lower risk of liver fibrosis and cirrhosis in people with existing liver conditions. Some research points to caffeine and plant compounds like chlorogenic acid as the drivers behind this effect.

This isn't medical advice, and coffee isn't a treatment for liver disease. But if you're already a coffee drinker, taking it black is a simple way to get the potential benefit without the added sugar and saturated fat that milk-heavy drinks bring along.

Here are 5 black coffees worth keeping in your rotation, and why each one works for a daily black cup.

### 1\. Koraput, Odisha Washed Coffee

A clean, bright single-origin from the hills of Koraput, Odisha. The fully washed process strips away the cherry skin and mucilage before drying, leaving a cup with well-defined acidity and none of the added fat or sugar that usually comes with a milk-based coffee. If you want your daily black coffee to actually taste good instead of just being medicine, this is where to start.

[![Koraput, Odisha Washed Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput-washed.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/koraput-odisha-washed-coffee)

### 2\. Karadykan Estate Coffee

Grown under native shade cover, this single-estate Arabica has a clean, well-balanced cup with notes of chocolate, citrus, nutty and orange. It's smooth enough to drink black every day without feeling like a chore, which matters more than any single "superfood" coffee - the liver-health research is about consistent, regular intake, not one perfect cup.

[![Karadykan Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/karadykan-estate-coffee)

### 3\. Biccode Estate Coffee

A washed-process Arabica (SLN 795) with notes of lemon zest, cacao nibs, caramel and toasted flavours. It's a medium-intensity cup, which makes it easy to drink two or three black coffees through the day without the harshness of a darker roast - useful if you're trying to build black coffee into a habit rather than an occasional treat.

[![Biccode Estate Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/biccode-estate-coffee)

### 4\. Halflong Assam Coffee

A single-origin Arabica from the North Cachar Hills of Assam, with mild acidity and a soft, earthy sweetness. It's gentler than most South Indian estate coffees, so it works well as an everyday black coffee for people who find brighter, more acidic cups hard on an empty stomach.

[![Halflong Assam Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fkoraput.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/halflong-assam-coffee)

### 5\. Basic Black Coffee

Our everyday, no-frills blend - smooth, balanced, and made to be brewed any way you like without fuss. If the goal is simply "drink black coffee consistently, without overthinking it," this is the most practical option: no single-origin ceremony, just a reliable cup you'll actually finish every day.

[![Basic Black Coffee](https://graycup.in/_next/image?url=%2Fproducts%2Fground-coffee.png&w=3840&q=75)](https://graycup.in/products/basic-black-coffee)

### How Much Black Coffee Is Reasonable?

Most of the research showing a liver benefit looked at people drinking somewhere between 2 and 4 cups of coffee a day. More isn't necessarily better - past a certain point, added caffeine mostly just affects sleep and anxiety rather than adding further benefit. If you're new to drinking coffee black, start with one cup and build up gradually.

### A Few Practical Notes

*   **Skip the sugar, go easy on the milk.** The liver-health studies are about coffee itself, not coffee as a vehicle for sugar and cream.
*   **Ground coffee is a better choice than instant.** Freshly brewed, ground coffee retains more of the chlorogenic acid and other plant compounds thought to drive the liver benefit - instant coffee loses some of these during processing. If liver health is your reason for drinking black coffee, brewing from ground beans is the more effective habit.
*   **Filter or pour-over both work.** There's no strong evidence that brew method changes the liver benefit - it's more about total intake over time.
*   **Talk to a doctor if you have existing liver disease.** Coffee is a helpful habit, not a substitute for medical care.

* * *

None of this is a reason to start drinking coffee if you don't already. But if black coffee is already part of your day, choosing beans you actually enjoy black - rather than only tolerating dark, bitter coffee out of duty - makes it far easier to keep the habit going.

### BEGIN PAGE
title: How to Brew the Perfect Cup of Tea | Gray Cup Guides
url: https://graycup.in/guides/brewing-the-perfect-cup
### END PAGE

A great cup of tea starts long before the kettle boils. From choosing the right leaf to knowing exactly when to pull your bag, every step matters. This guide walks you through everything you need to know.

### 1\. Start With Good Water

Tea is over 99% water, so quality matters. Use filtered or fresh tap water whenever possible - avoid re-boiled water, which loses dissolved oxygen and makes tea taste flat.

**Soft water** (low mineral content) tends to produce a brighter, more delicate cup. **Hard water** can dull the flavour and leave residue in your cup. If your tap water tastes good on its own, it'll make good tea.

### 2\. Get the Temperature Right

One of the most common mistakes is using boiling water for every type of tea. Different teas have different ideal temperatures:

*   **Black tea (CTC or loose leaf)** - 95–100°C. Full boil is fine.
*   **Green tea** - 70–80°C. Boiling water will make it bitter.
*   **White tea** - 75–85°C. Gentle heat preserves delicate flavour.
*   **Herbal infusions** - 95–100°C. Most herbs need full heat to release.

If you don't have a thermometer, boil the water and let it sit for 2–3 minutes before pouring over green or white teas.

### 3\. Measure Your Tea

Too much or too little tea changes everything.

*   **Loose leaf tea** - 2–3 grams per 200 ml (roughly 1 heaped teaspoon)
*   **Tea bags** - 1 bag per cup is standard
*   **CTC granule tea** - 1 teaspoon per cup, or slightly more for a strong chai

When in doubt, start lighter and adjust to taste. You can always steep longer or add more leaves next time.

### 4\. Steeping Time

Steeping time is where most people go wrong. Too short and the tea is thin; too long and it turns bitter.

*   **Black CTC tea** - 3–5 minutes
*   **Loose leaf black tea** - 3–4 minutes
*   **Green tea** - 1–3 minutes
*   **White tea** - 2–4 minutes
*   **Herbal tea** - 5–7 minutes

Taste as you go. The perfect steep time is the one that works for your palate.

### 5\. Brewing Methods

#### Teapot or Cup Infuser

The classic approach. Add loose leaves to a strainer or infuser basket, pour hot water over them, steep, and remove. A teapot is ideal for multiple cups since the ratio stays consistent.

#### Chai-Style (Milk Tea)

Popular across India, this method involves simmering tea leaves or granules directly in water and milk together. Add your CTC tea to cold water, bring to a boil, then add milk and simmer for 2–3 minutes. Strain and serve.

This method extracts more from the leaf and produces a richer, thicker cup - perfect for strong morning tea.

#### Cold Brew

Cold brewing produces a smoother, naturally sweeter tea with less bitterness. Add 1 tablespoon of loose leaf tea per 500 ml of cold water, refrigerate for 8–12 hours, strain, and serve over ice.

### 6\. Small Details That Make a Big Difference

*   **Warm your cup first** by rinsing it with hot water before pouring. This keeps the tea from cooling too fast.
*   **Don't squeeze the bag** - it releases bitter tannins into the cup.
*   **Use a lid while steeping** loose leaf tea to retain heat and aromatics.
*   **Fresh leaves matter** - older teas lose volatile aromatics quickly. Store in an airtight container away from light.

* * *

The best cup of tea is the one you enjoy. Use this as a starting point and adjust every variable - temperature, time, leaf quantity - until it's exactly right for you.

---

### BEGIN PAGE
title: CTC vs Loose Leaf Tea: What's the Difference? | Gray Cup Guides
url: https://graycup.in/guides/ctc-vs-loose-leaf-tea
### END PAGE

Walk into any Indian kitchen and you'll find CTC tea. Walk into a specialty tea shop and you'll find rows of loose leaf. Both are tea - but they're made differently, taste differently, and suit different moments. Here's everything you need to know.

CTC stands for **Crush, Tear, Curl** - a mechanical process invented in the 1930s to make tea production faster and more consistent. Fresh tea leaves are passed through cylindrical rollers with serrated teeth that crush, tear, and curl them into small granules or pellets.

The result is a dense, uniform product that:

*   Brews quickly (2–4 minutes)
*   Produces a strong, bold, dark liquor
*   Holds up well in milk
*   Is more affordable per cup

CTC is the backbone of Indian chai culture. The granules extract rapidly in hot water and milk, producing that characteristic thick, malty brew. Assam CTC is the most widely consumed tea in India.

### What Is Loose Leaf Tea?

Loose leaf tea refers to whole or gently broken tea leaves that retain their natural structure after processing. Rather than being mechanically shredded, they're rolled, oxidised, and dried while staying largely intact.

Loose leaf teas include:

*   **Darjeeling first and second flush**
*   **Assam orthodox**
*   **Nilgiri teas**
*   **Green and white teas**
*   **Oolongs**

Because the leaves are whole, they expand significantly when steeped - releasing flavour gradually and producing a more complex, nuanced cup.

### How They Compare

#### Flavour

**CTC** produces a bold, robust, slightly bitter cup with a malty character. The strong flavour cuts through milk and sugar easily, which is why it's ideal for chai. It's consistent - one batch tastes much like another.

**Loose leaf** tends to be more layered. A good Darjeeling might have muscatel (grape-like) notes. An Assam orthodox can have earthy, brisk character. The flavour changes with steeping time, temperature, and even the time of harvest.

#### Brewing

**CTC** is forgiving. Toss a teaspoon in a pot, add water and milk, simmer for a few minutes. It's hard to ruin.

**Loose leaf** rewards attention. You need the right temperature, the right steeping vessel (a pot with a strainer or infuser), and the right time. Over-steep and it turns bitter. Get it right and it's worth it.

#### Quality and Price

CTC is more affordable because the production process is automated and the leaves don't need to be as carefully handled. Loose leaf, especially from premium estates, costs more - but you're also getting more from the leaf in terms of flavour.

It's worth noting that CTC teas from quality estates can be excellent. Price doesn't always mean better tea; it means different tea.

#### Which Holds Up in Milk?

CTC, without question. The strong tannins and bold flavour of CTC teas stand up to the fat and proteins in milk. Most loose leaf teas - especially delicate greens or first flush Darjeelings - are meant to be drunk plain. Adding milk to them masks the very character you're paying for.

### When to Choose CTC

*   You want a strong morning cup that works with milk
*   You're making chai with spices
*   You want consistency and value
*   You're making tea for a crowd

### When to Choose Loose Leaf

*   You want to explore tea as a flavour experience
*   You're drinking plain, without milk
*   You're brewing green, white, or specialty black teas
*   You want to slow down and pay attention to the cup

* * *

Neither is better. They're different tools for different situations. At Gray Cup, we stock both - because a good chai in the morning and a thoughtful Darjeeling in the afternoon are both worth having.

### BEGIN PAGE
title: Instant Coffee vs Brewed Coffee: Which Is Right for You? | Gray Cup Guides
url: https://graycup.in/guides/instant-vs-brewed-coffee
### END PAGE

Instant coffee gets a bad reputation. For years it was synonymous with weak, bitter, chemical-tasting drinks served at office meetings. That's changed significantly. At the same time, brewed coffee has never been more accessible. So which should you be drinking?

The honest answer: it depends on what you're looking for.

Instant coffee starts as brewed coffee. The liquid is either **spray-dried** (hot air evaporates the water, leaving behind fine powder) or **freeze-dried** (the brewed coffee is frozen into slabs, then the ice is removed under vacuum, leaving granules intact).

Freeze-dried instant coffee preserves more volatile aromatics - which is why freeze-dried products often taste noticeably better than spray-dried ones.

You dissolve it in hot or cold water (or milk), and you're done. No equipment, no mess, no waiting.

### What Is Brewed Coffee?

Brewed coffee involves forcing hot water through ground coffee beans. The most common methods:

*   **Filter / Pour-over** - hot water poured through ground coffee and a filter
*   **French press** - grounds steep in water, then are pressed to the bottom
*   **Moka pot** - pressurised steam pushes water through grounds on the stovetop
*   **Espresso machine** - high-pressure water through finely ground coffee
*   **Cold brew** - coarse grounds steeped in cold water for 12–24 hours

Each method produces a different flavour profile. The common thread: fresh grounds, ground close to brewing time, make significantly better coffee.

### The Honest Flavour Comparison

Good brewed coffee from quality beans has layers - acidity, sweetness, body, and aroma - that are genuinely complex. Even a simple pour-over with freshly ground beans will be noticeably more flavourful than most instant options.

Instant coffee, even good instant coffee, loses some of those volatile aromatics during processing. The high heat of spray-drying in particular damages the compounds responsible for brightness and complexity.

That said, **quality instant coffee is genuinely good**. Modern freeze-dried products from specialty roasters are miles ahead of what was available a decade ago. They make a solid cup - especially when you need one fast, are travelling, or are making an iced coffee drink where the coffee is diluted with milk and sugar anyway.

### Convenience vs Quality

This is the real trade-off.

**Instant coffee** wins on:

*   Speed (30 seconds, no equipment)
*   Portability (take it anywhere)
*   Consistency (same result every time)
*   No cleanup
*   Lower cost per cup in many cases

**Brewed coffee** wins on:

*   Flavour depth and complexity
*   Freshness
*   Control over strength and extraction
*   The experience of the ritual itself

### When Instant Makes Sense

*   Early mornings when you need caffeine, not ceremony
*   Travel, camping, or anywhere equipment isn't practical
*   Iced lattes and coffee-based drinks where coffee is one ingredient among many
*   Office situations where a full brew setup isn't available

### When to Brew

*   When the coffee itself is what you're tasting
*   Weekend mornings with time to spare
*   When you've invested in good beans and want to get the most from them
*   When you're developing a palate for coffee flavour differences

* * *

There's no wrong answer here. A good instant coffee in the right moment beats mediocre brewed coffee from stale beans. Know what you're optimising for - and keep both on hand.

### BEGIN PAGE
title: Gray Cup | Premium Indian Tea, Coffee & Matcha
url: https://graycup.in/how-to-use
### END PAGE

### How to Use

Select the grind size you bought and follow the steps below to brew it right.

### French Press

Full-bodied and rich, brewed by steeping coarse grounds directly in hot water.

1.  1Add 1 heaped tbsp of coarse-ground coffee per 200 ml of water to the French press.
2.  2Pour hot water (just off the boil, ~95°C) over the grounds and stir gently.
3.  3Place the lid on with the plunger pulled up, and let it steep for 4 minutes.
4.  4Press the plunger down slowly and evenly.
5.  5Pour and serve immediately - coffee left on the grounds keeps brewing and turns bitter.

Tips

*   • Grounds that are too fine will clog the mesh filter - stick to a coarse, sea-salt-like grind.
*   • Rinse the plunger and mesh filter right after brewing so oils don't build up and turn rancid.

### 3 Products

### Good to know

![](https://graycup.in/coffee-tree.svg)

Flavour notes describe the tastes and aromas you might pick up in the cup - similar to tasting notes on wine or whisky. They come from the coffee's origin, processing method, and roast, and are a guide to what to expect rather than a guarantee of what you'll taste.

Honey/semi-dry process - some mucilage is left on during drying, balancing brightness and sweetness.

How to UseHow to UseHow to UseHow to UseHow to UseHow to Use

How to UseHow to UseHow to UseHow to UseHow to UseHow to Use

### French Press

Full-bodied and rich, brewed by steeping coarse grounds directly in hot water.

1.  1Add 1 heaped tbsp of coarse-ground coffee per 200 ml of water to the French press.
2.  2Pour hot water (just off the boil, ~95°C) over the grounds and stir gently.
3.  3Place the lid on with the plunger pulled up, and let it steep for 4 minutes.
4.  4Press the plunger down slowly and evenly.
5.  5Pour and serve immediately - coffee left on the grounds keeps brewing and turns bitter.

Tips

*   • Grounds that are too fine will clog the mesh filter - stick to a coarse, sea-salt-like grind.
*   • Rinse the plunger and mesh filter right after brewing so oils don't build up and turn rancid.

### BEGIN PAGE
title: Gray Cup | Premium Indian Tea, Coffee & Matcha
url: https://graycup.in/return-policy
### END PAGE

Last updated: August 10, 2026

### General Policy

Gray Cup sells perishable food products (tea, coffee, and related goods), so we do not accept general change-of-mind returns. We do not offer returns or refunds simply because you no longer want an item you ordered.

### When a Refund Is Available

We will issue a refund or replacement if your order arrives damaged, spoiled, defective, or otherwise not fit for consumption, or if there was an error on our part in fulfilling your order. Contact us within a reasonable time of delivery with your order number and a description (and photos, where relevant) of the issue, and we will review your claim.

### How Refunds Are Issued

Approved refunds are issued to your original payment method through our payment processor. Once approved, refunds may take up to 7-10 business days to reflect, depending on your bank or payment provider.

### Repeated Refund Claims

Refund claims are reviewed individually and in good faith. However, if a customer repeatedly reports issues with orders that do not reflect a verifiable product or service problem, we reserve the right to decline further refund requests and, after three such claims, to stop accepting future orders from that customer.

### How to Request a Refund

Email your order number and the issue with your order to [office@graycup.org](mailto:office@graycup.org). We will get back to you with next steps.
